assets.label: Cash, interbank and central bank deposits

liabilities.label: Bank deposits, repos and bonds issued

balance.note: A bank's balance sheet is mostly other people's money: customer deposits fund the loans. Shareholders' funds are about 9% of assets, which is why capital ratios matter.

safety.label: CET1 capital ratio
safety.plain: The bank's own capital as a cushion against losses, as a share of its risk-weighted loans. Bank Negara's minimum is 4.5% plus buffers. As printed in the report's capital note; some banks print it before deducting the proposed dividend.

safety.label: Total capital ratio
safety.plain: All qualifying capital as a share of risk-weighted loans; the regulatory minimum is 8% plus buffers.

safety.label: Gross impaired loans
safety.plain: Loans in trouble as a share of all loans. Lower is better.

safety.label: Loan loss allowance coverage
safety.plain: Money already set aside for losses, compared with the troubled loans. Above 100% means fully covered.

safety.label: Loan to deposit ratio
safety.plain: The bank lends out about RM98 of every RM100 deposited.

safety.label: CASA ratio
safety.plain: Share of deposits in current and savings accounts, which pay little interest and keep funding cheap.

safety.label: Liquidity coverage ratio
safety.plain: Cash and easy-to-sell assets against 30 days of stressed outflows; the minimum is 100%.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM119.7 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM11 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (dividends paid in the last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM6.5 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM74 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.3 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM11 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin 1H2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM35.39.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Cost to income (1H2026)
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 of income, about RM50 is spent on staff, branches and IT. Lower is more efficient.

metrics.label: Credit cost (1H2026, annualised)
metrics.plain: Provisions for bad loans equal to 0.24% of loans a year. Lower is better.

drivers.evidence: Other operating income fell 15.4% to RM4.04bn in 1H2026 on mark-to-market losses and lower foreign-exchange gains (Q B1)
drivers.why: Market-related income swings with bond prices and currencies.

drivers.evidence: Net interest and Islamic banking income rose 1.6% to RM10.84bn in 1H2026 (Q B1)
drivers.why: Its core lending income keeps growing slowly.

drivers.evidence: Insurance/takaful service result fell 21.7% to RM677.9m in 1H2026 (Q B1)
drivers.why: Etiqa adds diversification but its earnings vary.

drivers.evidence: Loans to customers grew 3.0% in the year to June 2026 (database)
drivers.why: More loans mean more interest income.

drivers.evidence: Provisions of RM798m in 1H2026 against RM808m a year earlier (database)
CET1 capital ratio of 15.7% before the declared dividend (Q notes)
drivers.why: Room to keep paying high dividends.

drivers.evidence: Management expects Malaysia GDP growth of 5.3%, Indonesia 5.3% and Singapore 5.2% in 2026 (Q B3 p.107)
drivers.why: Its three home markets are all expected to grow.

drivers.evidence: Focus on Islamic finance, wealth, payments and corporate and investment banking, plus technology, data and AI (Q B3)
drivers.why: Execution will decide whether fee income grows.

outlook.text: Malaysia's outlook remains constructive: GDP growth projected at 5.3% in 2026, with the OPR expected to stay at 2.75% (Q B3 p.107).
Growth priorities: regional Islamic finance, wealth management, transactions and payments, and corporate and investment banking (Q B3).
Global growth expected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026; Middle East supply disruptions may push inflation up (Q B3).

outlookOverall.text: Management sees resilient growth across its ASEAN markets in 2026 and keeps investing in technology and capital efficiency (Q B3 p.107).
